answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small, time-locked stake before it can transact. Like water pooling in a lagoon, the stake sits visible and verifiable while honest work flows over it; fake identities built on shale-thin collateral are washed out, because spinning up thousands of them multiplies the cost faster than the reward. A peer reputation ridge — a durable record of fulfilled contracts — then raises the climb for newcomers, so one real agent with history outcompetes a swarm of cheap copies.
